title: Atomic Primitives
goal: Share and mutate primitive types across threads without a Mutex.

sections.text: Atomic types like `AtomicBool` and `AtomicI32` provide thread-safe interior mutability. You will recognise atomic variables from C++ or Java.

sections.caption: fetch_add mutates through a shared reference &AtomicI32.

sections.text: Unlike standard primitive types, atomic types allow mutation through a shared reference `&T`. You do not need `&mut` or a `Mutex`.
Every atomic operation requires an explicit `Ordering` argument. Memory orderings are covered later in this deck.

sections.caption: load returns a copy of the primitive value inside.

sections.text: Atomic types only exist for primitives and raw pointers. Complex structs still require a `Mutex` or `RwLock`.

explanation: Share and mutate primitive types across threads without a Mutex.
